Date: 2023-02-22
REMARKS
Claims 1-17 and 19-20 are pending in the present application. Claim 1 is amended in this paper. Claim 18 is canceled in this paper. No new claims are added in this paper.
In taking the foregoing actions, Applicant respectfully submits Applicant is not necessarily conceding in this application that these claims, as originally presented, are not patentable over the references cited by the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO), as pertinent ones of the present claim amendments and cancellations are only for facilitating expeditious prosecution. Applicant respectfully reserves the right to pursue the canceled claims and/or other claims in one or more continuing applications.
AFCP 2.0 Submission
This response after final is hereby provided as an AFCP 2.0 submission. Independent claim 1 has been amended in a non-broadening manner to recite allowable subject matter. Therefore, the limitations of the claims as amended constitute limitations previously considered in preparation of the instant office action, and thus do not raise new issues that would require further consideration and/or search. Applicant furthermore respectfully submits that the claims as presented herein place the application in condition for allowance as discussed below. See MPEP § 714.12; see also Guidelines for Consideration of Responses after Final Rejection under 37 CFR 1.116(b) under the After Final Consideration Pilot 2.0 (AFCP 2.0), available at https://www.uspto.gov/sites/default/files/patents/initevents/afcpguidelines.pdf Accordingly, Applicant respectfully submits that this paper represents a valid AFCP 2.0 submission, and requests that the claims as presented herein be allowed; Applicant further requests an interview pursuant to the AFCP 2.0 program guidelines to discuss this matter.
Allowable Subject Matter
The Office asserts at page 8 of the Office Action that claim 18 is "objected to as being dependent upon a rejected base claim, but would be allowable if rewritten in independent form including all of the limitations of the base claim and any intervening claims."
Solely in the interest of advancing prosecution, independent claim 1 has been amended to include the allowable subject matter of claim 18.
Obiections to the Drawings
The Office has objected to the drawings under 37 C.F.R. §1.83(a) as allegedly failing to "show every feature of the invention specified in the claims." (Office Action, p. 2) Applicant respectfully traverses the objection to the drawings under 37 C.F.R. §1.83(a). In particular, Applicant notes that, as outlined in MPEP 608.02 Drawing [R-07.2015], the statutory requirement for showing the claimed invention only requires that the "applicant shall furnish a drawing where necessary for the understanding of the subject matter to be patented..." (See 35 U.S.C. 113, See also 37 CFR §1.81(a), which states "[t]he applicant for a patent is required to furnish a drawing of the invention where necessary for the understanding of the subject matter sought to be patented...").
In the pending application, Applicant respectfully submits that an express illustration of the limitations of "chamber," "inner wall," and "outer wall" of claim 19 as presented is not necessary for understanding by one of ordinary skill in the art of the subject matter to be patented. Accordingly, withdrawal of this objection is respectfully requested.
Reiection of claims under 35 U.S.C. 103
Epstein/Glaser
Claims 1, 6-11, 13-17 and 20 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly unpatentable over U.S. Patent Appl. Publ. No. 20150344143 Al to Epstein et al. (hereinafter "Epstein"), and further in view of U.S. Patent Appl. Publ. No. 20110042520 Al to Glaser et al. (hereinafter "Glaser"). Applicant respectfully traverses the rejection.
Claim 1
Claim 1 as amended includes allowable subject matter as noted above, reciting:
A method for fueling and using an aircraft, wherein the method comprises: storing, using a fuel tank, liquified gas fuel; fueling over a period of time exceeding 30 minutes, using a fuel line, an aircraft, wherein fueling further comprises: filling the fuel tank with liquified gas fuel to a desired level, wherein the desired level comprises fuel for a plurality of flights plus reserves, wherein a sensor connected to the fuel tank detects at least abnormal phenomena related to the fuel tank, wherein the sensor converts the detected at least abnormal phenomena into a signal that is then transmitted to a computing device; and
removing, using the computing device, the fuel line as function of the desired level in the aircraft; and preparing the fuel tank for flight as a function of the desired level; and flying, using the aircraft, a plurality of flights using the liquid gas fuel.
Accordingly, Applicant respectfully submits that claim 1 is patentably distinguishable over Epstein and Glaser, alone or in combination, for at least the reasons discussed above.
Claims 6-11, 13-17 and 20
Each of claims 6-11, 13-17 and 20 as presented depends, directly or indirectly, from claim 1. As noted above, claim 1 is patentably distinguishable over Epstein and Glaser, alone or in combination, for at least the reasons discussed above. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully submits that claims 6-11, 13-17 and 20 as presented are patentably distinguishable over Epstein and Glaser, alone or in combination, for at least the reasons discussed above.
Epstein/Glaser/D'Auvergne
Claim 2 stands rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly unpatentable over Epstein, in view of Glaser, and further in view of U.S. Patent No. 7281682 B2 to D'Auvergne. Applicant respectfully traverses the rejection.
Claim 2 as presented depends directly from claim 1. As noted above, claim 1 as amended recites allowable subject matter. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully submits that claim 2 as presented is patentably distinguishable over Epstein, Glaser, and D'Auvergne, alone or in combination, for at least the reasons discussed above.
Epstein/Glaser/Wexler
Claims 3 and 5 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly unpatentable over Epstein, in view of Glaser, and further in view of U.S. Patent No. 6123295 A to Wexleret al. (hereinafter "Wexler"). Applicant respectfully traverses the rejection.
Each of claims 3 and 5 as presented depends, directly or indirectly, from claim 1. As noted above, claim 1 as amended recites allowable subject matter. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully submits that claims 3 and 5 as presented are patentably distinguishable over Epstein, Glaser, and Wexler, alone or in combination, for at least the reasons discussed above.
Epstein/Glaser/Clark
Claims 4 and 19 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly unpatentable over Epstein, in view of Glaser, and further in view of U.S. Patent No. 6422514 Bl to Clark et al. (hereinafter "Clark"). Applicant respectfully traverses the rejection.
Each of claim 4 and 19 as presented depends, directly or indirectly, from claim 1. As noted above, claim 1 as amended recites allowable subject matter. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully submits that claim 4 and 19 as presented are patentably distinguishable over Epstein, Glaser, and Clark, alone or in combination, for at least the reasons discussed above.
Epstein/Glaser/Benassi
Claim 12 stands rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly unpatentable over Epstein, in view of Glaser, and further in view of U.S. Patent Appl. Publ. No. 20120119032 Al to Benassi et al. (hereinafter "Benassi"). Applicant respectfully traverses the rejection.
Claim 12 as presented depends, directly or indirectly, from claim 1. As noted above, claim 1 as amended recites allowable subject matter. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully submits that claim 12 as presented is patentably distinguishable over Epstein, Glaser, and Benassi, alone or in combination, for at least the reasons discussed above.
Conclusion
Accordingly, Applicant respectfully submits that all claims in the application are in a condition for allowance and respectfully solicit the prompt issuance of a Notice of Allowance. If any issues remain, the Examiner is encouraged to call the undersigned practitioner at the number listed below.
Respectfully submitted, /Princess Onwuzuligbo/ Princess Onwuzuligbo
